"This tree species is a major honey plant in the eastern United States, yielding a dark reddish, fairly strong honey which gets mixed reviews as a table honey but is favorably regarded by bakers; nectar is produced in the orange part of the flowers.

Wood
 Very widely used where a cheap, easy-to-work and stable wood is needed. It is clearly the wood of choice for use in organs, due to its ability to take a fine, smooth, precisely cut finish and so to effectively seal against pipes and valves. It is also commonly used for siding clapboards. Its wood may be compared in texture, strength, and softness to white pine.

Used for interior finish of houses, for siding, for panels of carriages, for coffin boxes, pattern timber, and wooden ware. During scarcity of the better qualities of white pine, tulip wood has taken its place to some extent, particularly when very wide boards are required.

It also has a reputation for being resistant to termites, and in the Upland South (and perhaps elsewhere) house and barn sills were often made of tulip poplar beams.

Arts

The tulip tree has been referenced in many poems and the namesakes of other poems, such as William Stafford's "Tulip Tree."[30] It is also a plot element in the Edgar Allan Poe short story "The Gold-Bug".[31]

Another form of art that the tulip tree is a major part of is wood carving. The tulip poplar can be very useful and has been one of the favorite types of trees for wood carving by sculptors such as Wilhelm Schimmel and Shields Landon Jones."

description:
Native 
TN and KY state tree
Magnolia Family

"This tree species is a major honey plant in the eastern United States, yielding a dark reddish, fairly strong honey which gets mixed reviews as a table honey but is favorably regarded by bakers; nectar is produced in the orange part of the flowers.

Wood
 Very widely used where a cheap, easy-to-work and stable wood is needed. It is clearly the wood of choice for use in organs, due to its ability to take a fine, smooth, precisely cut finish and so to effectively seal against pipes and valves. It is also commonly used for siding clapboards. Its wood may be compared in texture, strength, and softness to white pine.

Used for interior finish of houses, for siding, for panels of carriages, for coffin boxes, pattern timber, and wooden ware. During scarcity of the better qualities of white pine, tulip wood has taken its place to some extent, particularly when very wide boards are required.

It also has a reputation for being resistant to termites, and in the Upland South (and perhaps elsewhere) house and barn sills were often made of tulip poplar beams.

Arts

The tulip tree has been referenced in many poems and the namesakes of other poems, such as William Stafford's "Tulip Tree."[30] It is also a plot element in the Edgar Allan Poe short story "The Gold-Bug".[31]

Another form of art that the tulip tree is a major part of is wood carving. The tulip poplar can be very useful and has been one of the favorite types of trees for wood carving by sculptors such as Wilhelm Schimmel and Shields Landon Jones."

Magnolia Family

"This tree species is a major honey plant in the eastern United States, yielding a dark reddish, fairly strong honey which gets mixed reviews as a table honey but is favorably regarded by bakers; nectar is produced in the orange part of the flowers.

Wood
 Very widely used where a cheap, easy-to-work and stable wood is needed. It is clearly the wood of choice for use in organs, due to its ability to take a fine, smooth, precisely cut finish and so to effectively seal against pipes and valves. It is also commonly used for siding clapboards. Its wood may be compared in texture, strength, and softness to white pine.

Used for interior finish of houses, for siding, for panels of carriages, for coffin boxes, pattern timber, and wooden ware. During scarcity of the better qualities of white pine, tulip wood has taken its place to some extent, particularly when very wide boards are required.

It also has a reputation for being resistant to termites, and in the Upland South (and perhaps elsewhere) house and barn sills were often made of tulip poplar beams.

Arts

The tulip tree has been referenced in many poems and the namesakes of other poems, such as William Stafford's "Tulip Tree."[30] It is also a plot element in the Edgar Allan Poe short story "The Gold-Bug".[31]

Another form of art that the tulip tree is a major part of is wood carving. The tulip poplar can be very useful and has been one of the favorite types of trees for wood carving by sculptors such as Wilhelm Schimmel and Shields Landon Jones."

description:
Native 
TN and KY state tree
Magnolia Family

"This tree species is a major honey plant in the eastern United States, yielding a dark reddish, fairly strong honey which gets mixed reviews as a table honey but is favorably regarded by bakers; nectar is produced in the orange part of the flowers.

Wood
 Very widely used where a cheap, easy-to-work and stable wood is needed. It is clearly the wood of choice for use in organs, due to its ability to take a fine, smooth, precisely cut finish and so to effectively seal against pipes and valves. It is also commonly used for siding clapboards. Its wood may be compared in texture, strength, and softness to white pine.

Used for interior finish of houses, for siding, for panels of carriages, for coffin boxes, pattern timber, and wooden ware. During scarcity of the better qualities of white pine, tulip wood has taken its place to some extent, particularly when very wide boards are required.

It also has a reputation for being resistant to termites, and in the Upland South (and perhaps elsewhere) house and barn sills were often made of tulip poplar beams.

Arts

The tulip tree has been referenced in many poems and the namesakes of other poems, such as William Stafford's "Tulip Tree."[30] It is also a plot element in the Edgar Allan Poe short story "The Gold-Bug".[31]

Another form of art that the tulip tree is a major part of is wood carving. The tulip poplar can be very useful and has been one of the favorite types of trees for wood carving by sculptors such as Wilhelm Schimmel and Shields Landon Jones."

description: This is a picture of a Tulip Tree (Liriodendron tulipifera), or Yellow Poplar as some people call it, that I observed while on a tree walk with the class last week. Tulip Trees can grow to incredible heights and are the tallest of all eastern hemlocks. The Tulip Tree has alternating leaves and the leaves have four lobes. Oftentimes people associate the leaf shape to look like a cat. They are also very broadleaf. On this tree, I did not get to observe the fruit it gives off, but I may be brown this time of year due to autumn being right around the corner. The twigs on a Tulip Tree are green, however, they will change to a browner color when the colder weather comes. The bark on this particular Tulip Tree was a grayish-brown color and lightly furrowed. Another tree species I saw around this area was a Horse Chestnut (Aesculus hippocastanum). The Horse Chestnut does not thrive in dry conditions and likes ample amounts of sunlight. On the other hand, the Tulip Trees like to grow in moist climates. So a moister climate would be good for both. The Tulip Tree grows in the USDA Plant Hardiness Zones 4 through 9, while the Horse Chestnut grows in zones 3 through 8. They have very similar growing conditions that they would be able to survive the PA winters. Another tree I observed around was the Honey Locust (Gleditsia triacanthos). The Honey Locust like to grow in areas that are well-drained and they fall in zones 4 through 9 on the USDA Plant Hardiness Zones, just like the Tulip Tree. All the tree species show that they would be able to survive the climate that PA provides. However, all these trees can be assumed to be deliberately planted by Slippery Rock University also being another reason why they can all be viewed in close proximity. The temperature on the day that I observed these species had a high of 72F and a low of 52F, however, the temperature at the time I observed them was 61F. It was a nice, sunny day out with light clouds at the time I observed with no precipitation at the time. There was the humidity of 77% and wind moving in an eastern direction at 6mph with a 20% chance of rain at some point in the day.
